producer_report.summary: Added decision D66 to docs/decisions.md and a one-line CHANGELOG note. Nothing else changed. D66 says the cause is in `landing` in crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs: it refuses any commit adding closing records for more than one job (lines 257-259). It also requires each job's candidate and verification fingerprint to equal the whole landed tree (lines 340-350). With several jobs in one squash, at most one could match. Design §7.3 describes a squash as one landing of one job. D66 compares four options: (a) exempt ee4b0dd, (b) teach the check to accept multi-job commits, (c) stop squashing multi-job PRs, (d) rewrite history. It recommends (c), plus (a) for the one existing commit, and says implementation is a follow-up awaiting the user's choice. It also says (c) is enforced only if the host restricts allowed merge methods.

checks_run.note: all tests passed; the three live tests that call a real model were ignored

open_issues: The cause is read from code and docs; I did not reproduce the failure or see its output.
Whether the failure is exactly the multi-job refusal on ee4b0dd is therefore inferred.
The brief's deliverables list also names docs/design/athena-v0.md, athena.toml and landing_tests.rs, but the acceptance criteria and out-of-scope list forbid changing them, so I left them untouched.
The user must choose (a), (b) or (c); the follow-up job needs the full id of ee4b0dd.
mistakes: I first tried a grep through Bash, which the policy denied. I switched to the Grep tool.
learnings: `landing` in invariant.rs refuses a commit that adds closing records for more than one job.
Each job's fingerprints must equal the whole landed tree's fingerprint, so (b) needs a new per-job content proof, not just removal of the one-job check.
Exemptions skip the whole invariant for one commit (invariant.rs lines 92-100); D60 and D61 govern them.
`Bash` allows no grep, so inspect files with the Grep tool.
desires: The full 40-character id of ee4b0dd, and the list of jobs it contains.
